target.title: feat: add autoreview model and speed defaults
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Autoreview could not select private/custom Codex model names or request Codex fast mode through stable personal defaults. Its public copy had also accumulated compatibility and isolation behavior that was missing from OpenClaw's vendored copy.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add generic model/config/speed overrides through environment variables while preserving reviewed-repository isolation. Reconcile the existing engine, Cursor, Copilot, and compatibility hardening so this repository remains the canonical source for OpenClaw's synchronized copy.

## User Impact

Users can keep personal defaults in shell or launcher environment, or repository-local defaults in an untracked environment loader such as `.envrc`. The helper itself does not write a defaults file.

Codex currently maps `fast` to the `priority` service tier and filters unsupported tiers against model metadata. A custom model name is accepted; fast mode only takes effect when its catalog entry advertises the tier.

## Evidence

- AI-assisted change; no transcript attached.
- `uv run --with pyyaml scripts/validate-skills`
- skill-creator `quick_validate.py skills/autoreview`
- `skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --self-test`
- `python3 skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview_test.py` (16 tests)
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s skills/autoreview/tests -p 'test_*.py'` (14 tests)
- A private custom model name plus `AUTOREVIEW_CODEX_SPEED=fast` dry-run verified model/config propagation.
- Full branch autoreview with `gpt-5.5` fast mode: clean, confidence 0.84.
- OpenAI Codex source checked at `be33f80bc65159c094ecd06bf155afa3061ce23d`: `ServiceTier::Fast` maps to `priority`; session setup filters tiers not advertised by model metadata.
